name: Zenith Earth Jukebox
about: Each track pairs a Moon or Mars base with its best Earth analog site. Two voices share one key and one chord; the Earth voice is detuned by how badly each measured dimension matches, so beating means a mismatch. See docs/SONIFICATION.md.

tracks.title: Shackleton crater rim (Moon) and Antarctica
tracks.mission: Crewed base at the lunar south pole that mines ice
tracks.description: Antarctica (Earth) beside Shackleton crater rim (Moon). Match 50%, so the chord is partly in tune, with slow beating; the least matched tone is surface brightness. Flat, smooth ground gives a narrow melody; the base's steep, very rugged ground gives a wide melody, at a steady pace. Bright ground gives a high, airy tone. Both places have ground ice, so two glassy bells ring together. Low sun at the base darkens its tone. The satellite view around the Earth site is white and cloudy, which shapes its voice.
tracks.how_to_listen: The base sits a little to the left, the Earth site a little to the right. Wobbling or beating between them means a mismatch.

frame.source: NASA Visible Earth Blue Marble (public domain), a stand-in for NASA Earth Information Center frames

tracks.title: Malapert Massif (Moon) and Pakistan
tracks.mission: Solar-powered lander on the Malapert ridge
tracks.description: Pakistan (Earth) beside Malapert Massif (Moon). Match 58%, so the chord is partly in tune, with slow beating; the least matched tone is sunlight. Steep, very rugged ground gives a wide melody, like the base, at a lively pace. Mid-tone ground gives a soft, mellow tone. Only the Earth site has ground ice, so only one glassy bell rings. Low sun at the base darkens its tone. The satellite view around the Earth site is sandy and clear, which shapes its voice.
tracks.how_to_listen: The base sits a little to the left, the Earth site a little to the right. Wobbling or beating between them means a mismatch.
